positions.commentary: Tesla is cited as an example of a company that can come back 80% and still be an expensive stock.
Netflix appears to have reached escape velocity, no longer needing to raise capital despite carrying significant debt.
The speaker was on the other side of Michael Burry's long position in GameStop and felt nervous about trading against him.
Amazon is cited as an example of a growth stock that never gets cheap because it is too good.
Microsoft is identified as a quality stock that gets picked up on multiple occasions through 2013.
Shopify is mentioned as a monster winner that will always be expensive because it is a great business.

thesis: This episode argues that 'escape velocity' is a critical threshold for growth stocks, noting that companies like Netflix and Microsoft have achieved it while others like Tesla and GameStop have not, creating a divergence in their investment cases. The speaker contends that value is currently compelling and defensive, suggesting it is difficult to see how value stocks would need to draw down further to reach parity with expensive growth stocks.

claims.quote: Tesla, maybe it gets to escape velocity. No, I don't think so. But I think that that basket of, you know, kind of junky fundamentals isn't enough.
